tasksTab.title: Tasks table
tasksTab.intro: The AI already detects many species reliably. Recordings that contain only such a species can be handled quickly here, many at once: the Tasks table is where operations on many tasks live, such as setting a status or replacing tags on all ticked tasks. This short lesson shows how to browse and preview recordings; afterwards it sends you back to Annotate.

steps.title: Tasks table
steps.hint: Every recording of the project is one row here, with its status badges.

steps.title: Move with ↑ ↓
steps.hint: `↓` and `↑` move the highlighted row. The list scrolls with it.

steps.title: Open a preview
steps.hint: Click an empty part of a row (not the recording name, which is a link) to open its spectrogram preview. Click it again to close it.
steps.task: Click an empty part of a row

steps.title: Pin previews
steps.hint: Press `p` to pin the open preview. Pinned previews stay open while you move on, up to 5 at once, so you can compare recordings.

steps.title: All shortcuts
steps.hint: Click {icon:help} or press `?` to see every shortcut of this table, then close the list with `Esc`. Tip: `Shift` + click ticks several rows. With rows ticked, `1`–`4` set Accepted, Unsure, Rejected or Verified on all of them at once.
steps.task: Open the shortcut list with `?`, then close it

steps.title: Back to Annotate
steps.hint: Some species need a closer look before you can identify them: listening, zooming in, checking each call. That is what the Annotate tab is for, and the lessons continue there. Click “Annotate” at the top of the page.

tasksTabLessons.title: Bulk actions
tasksTabLessons.intro: The AI already recognises the common pipistrelle (Pipistrellus pipistrellus) very reliably. Recordings with only this species don't need to be opened one by one: here you check and process many at once. 20 such recordings were added to your tour for this (task tag “tour: bulk”).

steps.title: Only the clear cases
steps.hint: Click {icon:filter} “Filters” and choose “Tag”. Under “Include”, add “species: Pipistrellus pipistrellus”. Then set “Distinct tags on task” to 1 and click “Done”. Only recordings whose sound events carry nothing but this species remain: 7.

steps.title: Accept them all
steps.hint: Open a few previews (click a row) to check the calls. Then click the “All 7” pill under the header checkbox: it selects every filtered recording, not only this page. Press `1` (Accepted) and confirm.

steps.title: Feeding buzzes
steps.hint: Change the filter: remove the species and the amount, and include “type: feeding-buzz” instead. 5 recordings remain. Their feeding buzzes are tagged with the call type, but not with the species yet.

steps.title: Add the species to the buzzes
steps.hint: Click “All 5”, then “Add tag to tagged” (`t`). Pick “type: feeding-buzz” as the tag to look for and add “species: Pipistrellus pipistrellus”. Every feeding buzz now carries the species, the other events stay as they are.
steps.task: Add the species to all feeding buzzes

steps.title: Accept the buzz recordings
steps.hint: Still filtered to feeding buzzes: click “All 5” and press `1` (Accepted).

steps.title: Tick rows yourself
steps.hint: “All N” takes every filtered recording. To take only some, tick them: click a row's checkbox, or move through the rows with `↓` and `↑` (the preview opens) and tap `Shift` to tick or untick the current row. Dragging over several rows ticks them all at once. `Esc` clears the selection.

steps.title: Social calls
steps.hint: Now the same for social calls: include “type: social-call” instead of the feeding buzz (7 recordings). Tick the 6 recordings without a badge yet (one holds a feeding buzz too and is accepted already), or simply click “All 7”: accepted recordings are skipped. Use “Add tag to tagged” (`t`) with “type: social-call” and “species: Pipistrellus pipistrellus”, then press `1` (Accepted). The selection stays after a tag action, so the status goes to the same recordings.
steps.task: Tag and accept the social call recordings

steps.title: A second species
steps.hint: Two recordings also hold a few calls tagged as another species, which are pipistrelle calls in fact. Include “species: Pipistrellus pipistrellus” and “species: Pipistrellus nathusii”, and choose “AND” under “Combine included tags with”. One recording remains: AND keeps out lesson recordings with only Nathusius' pipistrelle.

steps.title: Replace the wrong species
steps.hint: Click “All 1”, then “Replace sound event tags” (`r`). Replace “species: Pipistrellus nathusii” with “species: Pipistrellus pipistrellus”.

steps.title: And the other one
steps.hint: In the filter, swap “species: Pipistrellus nathusii” for “species: Nyctalus leisleri” (still AND with “species: Pipistrellus pipistrellus”). Click “All 1”, then replace “species: Nyctalus leisleri” with “species: Pipistrellus pipistrellus”.

steps.title: Accept the last two
steps.hint: Both recordings now carry only the pipistrelle. Filter again: include “species: Pipistrellus pipistrellus”, “Distinct tags on task” 1. The two appear next to the 7 accepted earlier. Click “All”, press `1` (Accepted).

steps.title: Clear the filters
steps.hint: Every bulk recording has a status badge now. Remove the filters again (the ✕ on each filter badge), so the table shows all recordings.

steps.title: Back to Annotate
steps.hint: Done: 20 recordings checked and processed without opening one of them. Click “Annotate” at the top to finish the Tags lesson.

steps.title: Welcome to Sonari
steps.hint: This tour teaches you to annotate recordings, in about 30 minutes and at your own pace. You need no prior experience with Sonari. Each recording is one lesson. The green frame always marks the part of the page the current step is about. Right now it frames the task bar: the current task, how many tasks remain and how many there are, the filters, and the arrows {icon:prev} {icon:next} to switch to the previous or next task. This card shows the current step and ticks it off when you have done it; collapse it with the arrow at the top any time.

steps.title: The recording
steps.hint: This row describes the recording you are working on. From the left: the file name (click it to download the recording); “(1/1)” counts the tasks of this recording: it is split into 1 task, and this is task 1. Longer recordings are split into several tasks. Then the date and time it was recorded, and its location (latitude and longitude). Click the location to see it on a map. Then the samplerate, 384,000 Hz: how many samples per second the recorder took. A high rate is what captures ultrasonic bat calls. Last comes the number of channels: 1 is mono.

steps.title: The spectrogram
steps.hint: The picture of the sound: time runs from left to right, frequency from bottom to top, and brighter means louder. Each box on it is a sound event: one call someone marked and tagged with its species. A box spans the call's duration and its frequency range. Annotating means checking these events, correcting them and adding missing ones.

steps.title: The action bar
steps.hint: All tools for the spectrogram live here, for example hide {icon:hide-spectrogram}, zoom {icon:zoom}, the sound event tools {icon:create} {icon:select} {icon:delete}, settings {icon:settings} and the player. Hover a button to see its shortcut. The next lessons use them one at a time.

steps.title: The Tasks table
steps.hint: Click “Tasks” at the top of the page. A short lesson of 6 steps runs there. When it is done, click “Annotate” to come back and continue here.

steps.title: Status badges
steps.hint: When you are done with a recording, give it a status badge. It saves your verdict and opens the next recording. In this tour, the next recording is also the next lesson. Any badge works here: click one or press `1`–`4`.
steps.task: Give this task any status badge

lessons.title: Listen
lessons.intro: Bat calls are ultrasonic. Played slowed down, they help you find calls and hear their rhythm. The species itself you identify from the call shape in the spectrogram.

steps.title: Play
steps.hint: Press `Space` or click {icon:play} to play and pause. Bat calls are ultrasonic, so Sonari plays them slowed down to make them audible.

steps.title: Speed
steps.hint: Change the speed in the {icon:speed} menu. Slower stretches the calls further and lowers their pitch.

steps.title: Repeat & autoplay
steps.hint: {icon:loop} repeats the visible part. {icon:autoplay} starts playback on every recording you open. A filled, ringed button is switched on.

steps.title: Seek
steps.hint: Double-click the spectrogram where playback should start. A red line shows the current position.

steps.title: Next lesson
steps.hint: Done with this recording. Give it any status badge: click one or press `1`–`4`. It opens the next recording and with it the next lesson.
steps.task: Give this task any status badge

lessons.title: Moving around
lessons.intro: Recordings are often longer than the screen. Moving quickly through them lets you check every call.

steps.title: Drag to pan
steps.hint: Click and drag the spectrogram sideways. Trackpad scroll gestures work too.

steps.title: Overview strip
steps.hint: This strip shows the whole recording. The green window marks the part you see above. Drag the window, or click anywhere in the strip to jump there.
steps.task: Click or drag in the overview strip

steps.title: Arrow keys
steps.hint: `←` and `→` move in time, `↑` and `↓` in frequency. With `Shift` held, `←` and `→` switch to the previous or next recording.

steps.title: Zoom in time
steps.hint: `+` and `-` zoom in and out in time, so you see a shorter or longer part of the recording at once. The next lesson shows more ways to zoom.

steps.title: Next lesson
steps.hint: Done with this recording. Give it any status badge: click one or press `1`–`4`. It opens the next recording and with it the next lesson.
steps.task: Give this task any status badge

lessons.title: Zoom
lessons.intro: Short and faint calls are easy to miss, and their shape is what tells species apart. Zooming in shows both.

steps.title: Zoom mode
steps.hint: Press `z` or click {icon:zoom} to switch on box zoom.

steps.title: Box zoom
steps.hint: Drag a rectangle around one call. The view zooms to exactly that area: now you see where the call starts and ends in frequency and how steeply it falls.

steps.title: Zoom in frequency
steps.hint: You know `+` and `-` for time already. Hold the Control key as well (Ctrl, also on a Mac) to zoom in frequency instead.

steps.title: Reset
steps.hint: Press `u` or click {icon:reset} to see the whole recording again.

steps.title: Next lesson
steps.hint: Done with this recording. Give it any status badge: click one or press `1`–`4`. It opens the next recording and with it the next lesson.
steps.task: Give this task any status badge

lessons.title: Sound events
lessons.intro: Sound events are the core of annotation: each one marks a call and carries its species.

steps.title: Create
steps.hint: The bright call at about 0.9 s (around 24–30 kHz) is not marked yet. Zoom in {icon:zoom} on it if it looks tiny. Then press `c` or click {icon:create} to switch on create mode and drag a box around it, from its start to its end and from its lowest to its highest frequency. The new event is selected right away.
steps.task: Draw a box around the call at 0.9 s

steps.title: Details
steps.hint: This panel shows the selected event: a zoomed preview, its tags and its measurements. Events created by an AI model also show how confident the model was.

steps.title: Tag your new event
steps.hint: Your new event has no tag yet: the Details panel shows an empty tag list. Press `a` or click “Add tags”, type “Nyctalus leisleri” and choose “species: Nyctalus leisleri”. A sound event without a species is unfinished.

steps.title: Deselect
steps.hint: `Esc` clears the selection.

steps.title: Select
steps.hint: Press `s` or click {icon:select}, then click an event. Drag its corners to make it fit the call.

steps.title: Jump between events
steps.hint: `n` jumps to the next event, `b` back to the previous one. No scrolling through long recordings.

steps.title: Jump to a tag
steps.hint: `m` only works with no event selected, so press `Esc` first. Then press `m` and choose the tag “this: is wrong”. It now shows at the top right of the spectrogram, and `n` and `b` only visit events with that tag. Press `n` to jump straight to the mislabeled event. Press `m` again later to visit all events again.
steps.task: Press `Esc`, then `m`, and choose “this: is wrong”

steps.title: Delete
steps.hint: The event at about 4.9 s, high up at 150 kHz, is tagged “this: is wrong”: it is not a call. It is selected after `n`: press `x`, or switch on delete mode {icon:delete} and click it.

steps.title: Undo
steps.hint: Deleted the wrong one? `Ctrl+z` brings it back. Undo works for events and tags. Try it now.

steps.title: Redo
steps.hint: `Ctrl+Shift+z` or `Ctrl+y` redoes it, so the mislabeled event is gone again.

steps.title: Next lesson
steps.hint: Done with this recording. Give it any status badge: click one or press `1`–`4`. It opens the next recording and with it the next lesson.
steps.task: Give this task any status badge

lessons.title: Tags
lessons.intro: Tags say what a sound event is. A wrong or missing species is the error you will fix most often.

steps.title: Remove a wrong tag
steps.hint: The event at about 1.6 s is tagged “this: is wrong” next to its species. Select it, then click that tag to remove it, or press `d` for a picker. Careful: `x` and delete mode {icon:delete} remove the whole event, `Ctrl+z` brings it back.

steps.title: Replace on all events
steps.hint: This recording is a Bechstein's bat (the file name ends in “Mbec”), and most events are tagged “species: Myotis bechsteinii”. But 16 events are tagged “species: Mbart”. Fix them all at once: press `Esc` so that no event is selected, press `r` and replace “species: Mbart” with “species: Myotis bechsteinii”. With no event selected, tag actions work on every event of the recording; with one selected, only on that one.

steps.title: Delete on all events
steps.hint: One event is tagged “species: Myotis daubentonii”. A second way to fix many events: with no event selected, press `d` and delete “species: Myotis daubentonii” from all events.

steps.title: Tag all untagged events
steps.hint: Now two events have no tag: the one you just cleared and one that never had a tag. Press `Shift+a` and add “species: Myotis bechsteinii” to all untagged events at once. Delete and add like this only when a recording holds a single species, as here.

steps.title: Task tags
steps.hint: Task tags describe the whole recording instead of one call, e.g. when a file holds only noise or insects. Add the tag “extra: test” here: click “Add tags” in the task tags, type `extra:test` and choose “Create the tag”. It is only a practice tag.

steps.title: Bulk actions on the Tasks tab
steps.hint: Fixing tags event by event is fine for a few recordings. For many, the Tasks table does it all at once. Click “Tasks” at the top: a lesson about bulk actions runs there. When it is done, click “Annotate” to come back here.

steps.title: Next lesson
steps.hint: Done with this recording. Give it any status badge: click one or press `1`–`4`. It opens the next recording and with it the next lesson.
steps.task: Give this task any status badge

lessons.title: View settings
lessons.intro: Every recorder and every species looks different. Adjusting the view makes faint calls stand out.

steps.title: Spectrogram settings
steps.hint: Press `o` or click {icon:settings}. Try another colormap or frequency range and watch the spectrogram change. “Save” keeps the settings for every recording and closes the panel; `o` or `Esc` closes it without saving.
steps.task: Open the settings, then close them

steps.title: Hide spectrogram
steps.hint: `h` or {icon:hide-spectrogram} hides spectrogram and waveform, e.g. to look at the events alone. Press it again to bring them back.

steps.title: Hide sound events
steps.hint: `Shift+h` or {icon:hide-events} hides the events, so you see the plain spectrogram. Show them again afterwards: only visible events can be selected and edited.

steps.title: Full page view
steps.hint: `w` or {icon:fullscreen} shows only the spectrogram, scaled to your screen. `w` again closes it.
steps.task: Open and close the full page view

steps.title: Shortcuts
steps.hint: Click {icon:help} or press `?` for every shortcut on this page. `Esc` closes the list.
steps.task: Open the shortcut list, then close it

steps.title: Next lesson
steps.hint: Done with this recording. Give it any status badge: click one or press `1`–`4`. It opens the next recording and with it the next lesson.
steps.task: Give this task any status badge

lessons.title: Practice
lessons.intro: Time to put it together on your own.

steps.title: Filters
steps.hint: Filters narrow down the recordings you work through, e.g. by date, time, station, tag or status badge. Press `f` or click {icon:filter} “Filters” and look through the list, then close it with `Esc`. During the tour, filters are not applied, so the lessons stay in order.

steps.title: Annotate on your own
steps.hint: All events in this recording are tagged soprano pipistrelle (Pipistrellus pygmaeus). Listen, check the calls, fix wrong tags and add missing calls. Then give the recording a status badge.
steps.task: Give this task any status badge

lessons.title: More practice
lessons.intro: One more recording on your own, with two species this time.

steps.title: Annotate on your own
steps.hint: Most events here are tagged Natterer's bat (Myotis nattereri), one is tagged Plecotus. Tip: `m` with “species: Plecotus” and then `n` jumps straight to it. Check the calls, fix what is wrong, then give the recording a status badge.
steps.task: Give this task any status badge

steps.title: Notes
steps.hint: Every recording has notes for questions, remarks or problems, visible to your team. Mark a note as an issue (shown in red) to flag a problem. Delete your own notes with the trash icon.

steps.title: Your feedback
steps.hint: How was the tour? Unclear steps, missing features, bugs, ideas: all welcome. Press `q` to jump into the note field, write your note and save it with `Shift+Enter`. `Esc` leaves the field.

steps.title: Tour complete
steps.hint: Well done! Click “Finish tour” to go back to the home page. You can continue or restart the tour there any time.

steps.hint: Task tags describe the whole recording instead of one call, e.g. when a file holds only noise or insects. Add the tag “extra: test” here: click “Add tags” in the task tags, type `extra:test` and choose “Create the tag”. It is only a practice tag.

steps.title: Next lesson
steps.hint: Done with this recording. Give it any status badge: click one or press `1`–`4`. It opens the next recording and with it the next lesson.
steps.task: Give this task any status badge

lessons.title: Replace tags
lessons.intro: Sometimes a whole tag is wrong, not just missing. Replace swaps it in one step instead of removing and adding.

steps.title: Listen first
steps.hint: One event is tagged Graureiher (grey heron). Play the recording with `Space` and listen whether you can hear a heron.

steps.title: Replace a tag
steps.hint: Select the Graureiher event, then press `r` and replace its tag with “this: is wrong”.

steps.title: All events at once
steps.hint: Add, delete and replace work on the selected event. With no event selected (`Esc` deselects), they work on every event of the recording. To change only one event, select it first: jump to it with `n`, or press `s` (or click {icon:select}) and then click it. `Ctrl+z` undoes any of them.

steps.title: Next lesson
steps.hint: Done with this recording. Give it any status badge: click one or press `1`–`4`. It opens the next recording and with it the next lesson.
steps.task: Give this task any status badge

lessons.title: View settings
lessons.intro: Every recorder and every species looks different. Adjusting the view makes faint calls stand out.

steps.title: Spectrogram settings
steps.hint: Press `o` or click {icon:settings}. Try another colormap or frequency range and watch the spectrogram change. “Save” keeps the settings for every recording and closes the panel; `o` or `Esc` closes it without saving.
steps.task: Open the settings, then close them

steps.title: Hide spectrogram
steps.hint: `h` or {icon:hide-spectrogram} hides spectrogram and waveform, e.g. to look at the events alone. Press it again to bring them back.

steps.title: Hide sound events
steps.hint: `Shift+h` or {icon:hide-events} hides the events, so you see the plain spectrogram. Show them again afterwards: only visible events can be selected and edited.

steps.title: Full page view
steps.hint: `w` or {icon:fullscreen} shows only the spectrogram, scaled to your screen. `w` again closes it.
steps.task: Open and close the full page view

steps.title: Shortcuts
steps.hint: Click {icon:help} or press `?` for every shortcut on this page. `Esc` closes the list.
steps.task: Open the shortcut list, then close it

steps.title: Next lesson
steps.hint: Done with this recording. Give it any status badge: click one or press `1`–`4`. It opens the next recording and with it the next lesson.
steps.task: Give this task any status badge

lessons.title: Practice
lessons.intro: Time to put it together on your own.

steps.title: Filters
steps.hint: Filters narrow down the recordings you work through, e.g. by date, time, station, tag or status badge. Press `f` or click {icon:filter} “Filters” and look through the list, then close it with `Esc`. During the tour, filters are not applied, so the lessons stay in order.

steps.title: Annotate on your own
steps.hint: Listen, check every event, fix wrong tags and add missing calls. Then give the recording a status badge.
steps.task: Give this task any status badge

steps.title: Notes
steps.hint: Every recording has notes for questions, remarks or problems, visible to your team. Mark a note as an issue (shown in red) to flag a problem. Delete your own notes with the trash icon.

steps.title: Your feedback
steps.hint: How was the tour? Unclear steps, missing features, bugs, ideas: all welcome. Press `q` to jump into the note field, write your note and save it with `Shift+Enter`. `Esc` leaves the field.

steps.title: Tour complete
steps.hint: Well done! Click “Finish tour” to go back to the home page. You can continue or restart the tour there any time.
